title: When the snow melts
predict: A warren lives on deep snow and most rabbits are white. The snow melts away. What happens to white fur over the next generations?
run: Press "Set up" (it plants a white-fur mutation on a snowy valley), let the white allele spread, then slide Snow down to 0 and run 5 generations.
explain: Use the cause-of-death graph: who is caught now, and why? Was white fur ever "good" on its own?

title: A cold snap
predict: Some rabbits have long ears, some short. A hard cold snap arrives. Which ear length do you expect to become more common, and what will the graph show?
run: Press "Set up", then run 8 generations. Watch the Allele frequency graph for e (long ears).
explain: Long ears lose body heat. Use the cause-of-death bars to point to the evidence for your explanation.

title: Woody food
predict: Grass dries and most of the food becomes tough and woody. Which teeth will help, and how fast will the change spread?
run: Press "Set up" and run 10 generations with the starting teeth dominance. Write down the long-teeth allele (T) frequency. Then press "Set up" again (it restarts the same seed) and, before pressing play, flip the teeth dominance in Controls > Genes. Run 10 generations again and compare.
explain: Only the dominance setting changed between the two runs. Why did the speed change? What happens to carriers when the mutant allele is recessive?

title: Do mutations appear on demand?
predict: Predators arrive. Will white-fur mutations appear because the rabbits need to hide? Predict how many mutations appear per new kit, with foxes and without them.
run: Press "Set up" (3 % mutation rate, foxes on). Open Controls > Genes and read the mutation counter, which lists the mutations and the new kits for each generation. Run 10 generations and write down mutations divided by new kits. Then press "Set up" again, switch the foxes off, run 10 generations and compare the ratios.
explain: Was the mutation rate higher when foxes made white fur useful? What does selection do with the mutations that already exist?

title: Chance and the bottleneck
predict: A storm wipes out 90 % of a large warren at random. Will the survivors have the same mix of alleles as before? Predict what happens to a rare allele.
run: Let the warren grow to 150+ with a high mutation rate, then press Bottleneck. Repeat from the same seed code and compare.
explain: Nothing about the survivors was "better". What is this called, and how is it different from natural selection?

title: Hidden carriers
predict: White fur is recessive. A few rabbits carry one white allele (Bb) but look brown. Will predators on grass remove the white allele completely?
run: Press "Set up", turn on Genotype view and run 15 generations, watching the Bb rabbits. For a comparison press "Set up" again, make white dominant in Controls > Genes before pressing play, and run 15 generations.
explain: A Bb rabbit stays brown, and a kit that inherits b from both parents is white. Where does the white allele hide, and how does it survive when bb rabbits are eaten? What changes when white is dominant?
